readings.title: The Genealogy of Saul
readings.subtitle: The House of Gibeon
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 9:35] And Ye‛i’ĕl the father of Giḇ‛on dwelt in Giḇ‛on, and his wife’s name was Ma‛aḵah. [36] And his first-born son was Aḇdon, then Tsur, and Qish, and Ba‛al, and Nĕr, and Naḏaḇ, [37] and Gedor, and Aḥyo, and Zeḵaryah, and Miqloth. [38] And Miqloth brought forth Shim‛am. And they also dwelt alongside their relatives in Yerushalayim, with their relatives. [39] And Nĕr brought forth Qish, and Qish brought forth Sha’ul, and Sha’ul brought forth Yehonathan, and Malkishua, and Aḇinaḏaḇ, and Eshba‛al.

readings.title: The Rebellion Begins
readings.subtitle: Jonathan Strikes the Philistine Garrison
readings.text: [1 Samuel 13:1] Sha’ul reigned one year, and when he had reigned two years over Yisra’ĕl, [2] Sha’ul chose for himself three thousand men of Yisra’ĕl. And two thousand were with Sha’ul in Miḵmash and in the mountains of Bĕyth Ěl, and a thousand were with Yehonathan in Giḇ‛ah of Binyamin. And the rest of the people he sent away, every man to his tent. [3] And Yehonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geḇa, and the Philistines heard of it. And Sha’ul blew the shophar throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Heḇrews hear!” [4] And all Yisra’ĕl heard the news that Sha’ul had struck a garrison of the Philistines, and also that Yisra’ĕl had become a stench to the Philistines. And the people were summoned to Sha’ul at Gilgal. [5] And the Philistines gathered to fight with Yisra’ĕl, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the seashore in multitude. And they came up and encamped in Miḵmash, to the east of Bĕyth Awen.

readings.title: A Disarmed Nation
readings.subtitle: The Lack of Blacksmiths in Israel
readings.text: [1 Samuel 13:19] Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Yisra’ĕl, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Heḇrews make swords or spears.” [20] And all Yisra’ĕl went down to the Philistines, each one to sharpen his ploughshare, and his mattock, and his axe, and his sickle. [21] And the charge for a sharpening was a pim for the ploughshares, and the mattocks, and the forks, and the axes, and to set the points of the goads. [22] And it came to be, on the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people who were with Sha’ul and Yehonathan. But they were found with Sha’ul and Yehonathan his son.

readings.title: Panic in the Camp
readings.subtitle: The People Hide in Caves
readings.text: [1 Samuel 13:6] And the men of Yisra’ĕl saw that they were in trouble, for the people were distressed, and the people hid in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in holes, and in pits. [7a] And some Heḇrews passed over the Yardĕn to the land of Gaḏ and Gil‛aḏ.

readings.title: Saul's Unlawful Sacrifice
readings.subtitle: The Kingdom Torn Away
readings.text: [1 Samuel 13:7b] As for Sha’ul, he was still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling. [8] And he waited seven days, according to the appointment with Shemu’ĕl. But Shemu’ĕl did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattered from him. [9] And Sha’ul said, “Bring a burnt offering and peace offerings here to me.” And he offered the burnt offering. [10] And it came to be, as he had finished offering the burnt offering, look, Shemu’ĕl came. And Sha’ul went out to meet him, to bless him. [11] And Shemu’ĕl said, “What have you done?” And Sha’ul said, “Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered together at Miḵmash, [12] so I said, ‘The Philistines are coming down on me at Gilgal, and I have not appeased the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ So I forced myself and offered a burnt offering.” [13] And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “You have acted foolishly. You have not guarded the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> commanded you. For now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would have established your reign over Yisra’ĕl forever. [14] “But now your reign is not going to stand. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall seek for <dn>Himself</dn> a man after <dn>His</dn> own heart, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall command him to be leader over <dn>His</dn> people, because you have not guarded what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded you.”

readings.title: Numbering the People
readings.subtitle: Raiders from the Philistine Camp
readings.text: [1 Samuel 13:15] And Shemu’ĕl arose and went up from Gilgal to Giḇ‛ah of Binyamin. And Sha’ul numbered the people present with him, about six hundred men. [16] And Sha’ul, and Yehonathan his son, and the people present with them remained in Giḇ‛ah of Binyamin, while the Philistines encamped in Miḵmash. [17] And raiders came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned onto the way to Ophrah, to the land of Shu‛al, [18] and another company turned onto the way to Bĕyth Ḥoron, and another company turned onto the way of the border that overlooks the Valley of Tseḇo‛im toward the wilderness.

readings.title: Jonathan's Daring Faith
readings.subtitle: No Restraint to Save by Many or by Few
readings.text: [1 Samuel 13:23] And the outpost of the Philistines went out to the pass of Miḵmash. [1 Samuel 14:1] And it came to be one day that Yehonathan son of Sha’ul said to the young man who bore his armour, “Come, let us go over to the outpost of the Philistines which is on the other side.” But he did not make it known to his father. [2] And Sha’ul was sitting in the outskirts of Giḇ‛ah under a pomegranate tree which is in Miḡron. And the people who were with him were about six hundred men. [3] And Aḥiyah son of Aḥituḇ, Ikaḇoḏ’s brother, son of Pineḥas, son of Ěli, the priest of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Shiloh, was wearing an ĕphod. But the people did not know that Yehonathan had gone. [4] And between the passes, by which Yehonathan sought to go over to the outpost of the Philistines, there was a sharp rock on one side and a sharp rock on the other side. And the name of one was Botsets, and the name of the other Seneh. [5] The one rock rose on the north opposite Miḵmash, and the other on the south opposite Geḇa. [6] And Yehonathan said to the young man who bore his armour, “Come, let us go over to the outpost of these uncircumcised. It might be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> works for us. For there is no restraint to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to save by many or by few.” [7] And his armour-bearer said to him, “Do all that is in your heart. Incline yourself. See, I am with you, according to your heart.” [8] And Yehonathan said, “See, we are passing over to the men, and we shall show ourselves to them. [9] “If they say thus to us, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we shall stand still in our place and not go up to them. [10] “But if they say thus, ‘Come up to us,’ then we shall go up. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given them into our hand, and this is the sign to us.” [11] And both of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines. And the Philistines said, “See, the Heḇrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden.” [12] And the men of the outpost answered Yehonathan and his armour-bearer, and said, “Come up to us, and let us show you a matter.” And Yehonathan said to his armour-bearer, “Come up after me, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given them into the hand of Yisra’ĕl.” [13] And Yehonathan climbed up on his hands and knees, and his armour-bearer after him. And they fell before Yehonathan. And as he went, his armour-bearer put them to death behind him. [14] And that first slaughter which Yehonathan and his armour-bearer made was about twenty men within about half an acre of land. [15] And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. The outpost and the raiders also trembled. And the earth shook, and it became a trembling of <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Battle Joined
readings.subtitle: Confusion in the Philistine Camp
readings.text: [1 Samuel 14:16] And the watchmen of Sha’ul in Giḇ‛ah of Binyamin looked and saw the crowd melting away, and they went here and there. [17] And Sha’ul said to the people who were with him, “Inspect now and see who has gone from us.” And they inspected and saw that Yehonathan and his armour-bearer were not there. [18] And Sha’ul said to Aḥiyah, “Bring the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> here,” for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was with the children of Yisra’ĕl on that day. [19] And it came to be, while Sha’ul talked to the priest, that the noise which was in the camp of the Philistines went on and increased. And Sha’ul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.” [20] And Sha’ul and all the people who were with him assembled, and they came to the battle. And see, every man’s sword was against his neighbour – a very great confusion. [21] And the Heḇrews who were with the Philistines before that, who went up with them into the camp all around, they also joined the Yisra’ĕlites who were with Sha’ul and Yehonathan. [22] And all the men of Yisra’ĕl who had hidden in the mountains of Ephrayim heard that the Philistines fled, and they also pursued them in the battle. [23] Thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved Yisra’ĕl that day, and the battle passed over to Bĕyth Awen.

readings.title: Saul's Rash Vow
readings.subtitle: Jonathan Rescued by the People
readings.text: [1 Samuel 14:24] And the men of Yisra’ĕl were distressed that day, for Sha’ul had placed the people under an oath, saying, “Cursed be the man who eats food until evening, and I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food. [25] And all those of the land came to a forest, and there was honey on the ground. [26] And the people came into the forest and saw the honey dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath. [27] But Yehonathan had not heard his father charging the people with the oath, so he stretched out the end of the rod that was in his hand and dipped it in a honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth. And his eyes were brightened. [28] And one of the people answered and said, “Your father strictly charged the people with an oath, saying, ‘Cursed be the man who eats food this day.’ ” And the people were faint. [29] And Yehonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. Look now, how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey. [30] “How much better if the people had eaten freely today of the spoil of their enemies which they found! For now, would there not have been a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?” [31] And they struck the Philistines that day from Miḵmash to Ayalon. And the people were very faint, [32] and the people rushed on the spoil, and took sheep, and cattle, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground. And the people ate with the blood. [33] And they told Sha’ul, saying, “Look, the people are sinning against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by eating with the blood!” And he said, “You have acted treacherously. Roll a large stone to me today.” [34] And Sha’ul said, “Disperse yourselves among the people, and say to them, ‘Bring me here every man’s ox and every man’s sheep, and slaughter them here and eat. And do not sin against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by eating with the blood.’ ” So every one of the people brought his ox with him that night, and slaughtered it there. [35] And Sha’ul built an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It was the first altar he built to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [36] And Sha’ul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and plunder them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them.” And they said, “Do whatever is good in your eyes.” Then the priest said, “Let us draw near to <dn>Elohim</dn> here.” [37] And Sha’ul asked of <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Do <dn>You</dn> give them into the hand of Yisra’ĕl?” But <dn>He</dn> did not answer him that day. [38] And Sha’ul said, “Come here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see what this sin has been today. [39] “For as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, who saves Yisra’ĕl, though it be in Yehonathan my son, he shall certainly die.” But not one among all the people answered him. [40] And he said to all Yisra’ĕl, “You be on one side, and my son Yehonathan and I be on the other side.” And the people said to Sha’ul, “Do what is good in your eyes.” [41] And Sha’ul said to <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, “Give a perfect lot!” And Sha’ul and Yehonathan were taken, but the people escaped. [42] And Sha’ul said, “Cast between my son Yehonathan and me.” And Yehonathan was taken. [43] And Sha’ul said to Yehonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” And Yehonathan told him, and said, “I indeed tasted a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand. Look, I die!” [44] And Sha’ul answered, “<dn>Elohim</dn> do so and more also, for you shall certainly die, Yehonathan.” [45] But the people said to Sha’ul, “Shall Yehonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Yisra’ĕl? Far be it! As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, let not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he has worked with <dn>Elohim</dn> this day.” So the people ransomed Yehonathan, and he did not die. [46] And Sha’ul went up from following the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.

readings.title: Summary of Saul's Reign
readings.subtitle: Wars and Family
readings.text: [1 Samuel 14:47] So Sha’ul took the reign over Yisra’ĕl, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Mo’aḇ, and against the children of Ammon, and against Eḏom, and against the sovereigns of Tsoḇah, and against the Philistines. And wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment. [48] And he gathered an army and struck the Amalĕqites, and delivered Yisra’ĕl from the hands of those who plundered them. [49] And the sons of Sha’ul were Yehonathan, and Yishwi, and Malkishua. And the names of his two daughters: the name of the first-born Mĕraḇ, and the name of the younger Miḵal. [50] And the name of Sha’ul’s wife was Aḥino‛am the daughter of Aḥima‛ats. And the name of the commander of his army was Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, Sha’ul’s uncle. [51] And Qish was the father of Sha’ul, and Nĕr the father of Aḇnĕr was the son of Aḇi’ĕl. [52] And the war against the Philistines was strong all the days of Sha’ul. And when Sha’ul saw any strong man or any brave man, he took him for himself.
